facts.statement: The genus Vytshegdus was named by Andreii Sennikov in 1988.
facts.quote: Vytshegdosuchus was named by Andreii Sennikov in 1988.

facts.statement: The genus contains only one known species, Vytshegdosuchus zheshartensis.
facts.quote: It contains a single species, Vytshegdosuchus zheshartensis.

facts.statement: Fossils of Vytshegdosuchus come from the Early Triassic (latest Olenekian stage) of the Komi Republic in Russia.
facts.quote: known from the Early Triassic (latest Olenekian stage) Yarenskian Gorizont of the Komi Republic of the European section of Russia.

facts.statement: The holotype of Vytshegdosuchus is a right ilium (PIN 3361/134), with a partial femur (PIN 3361/127) possibly serving as a paratype.
facts.quote: Vytshegdosuchus is known from the holotype PIN 3361/134, a right ilium, and possibly from the paratype PIN 3361/127, a partial femur.

facts.statement: Specimens were found in the Zheshart locality along the Vychegda River within the Parotosuchus fauna of the Upper Yarenskian Gorizont.
facts.quote: These specimens were collected from the a fossil assemblage called the Parotosuchus fauna of the Upper Yarenskian Gorizont, in the Zheshart locality along the Vychegda River in Aikino district of the Komi Republic.

facts.statement: The holotype represents the oldest known archosaur material from Russia and the only one from the Early Triassic period.
facts.quote: The holotype of Vytshegdosuchus is also the oldest material currently considered as belonging to Archosauria from Russia, and the only from the Early Triassic.

facts.statement: A 2011 numerical phylogenetic analysis by Nesbitt placed Vytshegdosuchus within the Paracrocodylomorpha.
facts.quote: A numerical phylogenetic analysis performed by Nesbitt (2011) placed it in the Paracrocodylomorpha.

facts.statement: Vytshegdosuchus was originally classified in the Rauisuchidae family based on similarities to other loricatan archosaurs.
facts.quote: Vytshegdosuchus was originally assigned to the Rauisuchidae based on comparisons with loricatans such as Rauisuchus, Saurosuchus and Arganasuchus.

facts.statement: The holotype ilium features a thickened ridge above the supra-acetabular crest, a trait found in many paracrocodylomorphs.
facts.quote: It preserved a thickened ridge dorsal to the supra-acetabular crest, which according to Nesbitt (2009) is a character only present in many paracrocodylomorphs.

facts.statement: The femur lacks an intertrochanteric fossa and has a low fourth trochanter, features consistent with proterosuchids, Euparkeria, and archosaurs.
facts.quote: The femur assigned to Vytshegdosuchus is consistent with proterosuchids, Euparkeria and archosaurs since, according to Gower and Sennikov (2000), it has no intertrochanteric fossa and a low fourth trochanter.

facts.statement: A groove on the proximal surface of the femur is a character shared with paracrocodylomorphs and some dinosauriforms.
facts.quote: Furthermore, the femur has a groove on its proximal surface, a character state found in paracrocodylomorphs, as well as some dinosauriforms.

facts.statement: Nesbitt (2009) suggested that Vytshegdosuchus is an archosaur belonging to the Paracrocodylomorpha.
facts.quote: Therefore, Nesbitt (2009) suggested that Vytshegdosuchus is an archosaur which is assignable to Paracrocodylomorpha.

facts.statement: It is debated whether isolated bones from widely separated localities can be confidently assigned to Vytshegdosuchus.
facts.quote: Nesbitt (2009) argued that the specimens referred to Vytshegdosuchus cannot unambiguously be assigned to that taxon, as these localities are well separated, and the bones were found isolated.

facts.statement: The Paleobi Database lists the parent group of Vytshegdosuchus as Paracrocodylomorpha.
